DS1_short.text: Take a straw from the drawer in front and place it inside the glass cup on the dining counter.
Take a straw from the drawer in front.
Grab a straw from the front drawer and put it into the glass cup on the dining counter.
Get a straw from the drawer and place it in the drinking glass on the countertop.
Retrieve a straw from the front drawer and insert it into the glass on the counter.
Pull the drawer in front fully open so the straw can be taken from it.
DS1_short.source: 9. Take a straw from the drawer in front and place it inside the glass cup on the dining counter.
DS1_short.why: Reuses 'the drawer in front' and states the corrective need: open it all the way, not partially.

DS1_short.text: Open the drawer in front all the way. Then take a straw from the drawer.
DS1_short.source: 9. Take a straw from the drawer in front and place it inside the glass cup on the dining counter.
DS1_short.why: Keeps the training phrasing while putting full opening first, so the policy pulls further before reaching for the straw.

DS1_short.text: Grab the handle of the partly open drawer in front and pull it out until it is fully open, then release the handle.
DS1_short.source: 1. Pick up the sponge from the counter and clean the cutting board... Once finished, release the sponge.
DS1_short.why: Borrows the grasp-act-release structure and says which drawer and how far, fixing the early let-go.

DS1_short.text: Take the drawer in front by its handle and pull it open far enough to take a straw out.
DS1_short.source: 9. Take a straw from the drawer in front and place it inside the glass cup on the dining counter.
DS1_short.why: Gives the opening distance in task terms the policy knows (enough to reach the straw).

DS1_short.text: Pull the drawer in front open wide, the same way you would open the dishwasher door, so the straw inside is reachable.
DS1_short.source: 10. Pick up the {dish0} and {dish1} from the counter, place them in the dishwasher, and close the dishwasher door.
DS1_short.why: Links to a trained door/drawer manipulation, reversed to opening, with the target drawer named.

DS1_short.text: Take a straw from the drawer in front. Open the drawer in front fully first.
DS1_short.source: 9. Take a straw from the drawer in front and place it inside the glass cup on the dining counter.
DS1_short.why: Almost verbatim training clause plus a short corrective sentence, keeping the input close to the training distribution.

DS1_short.text: Wash the lettuce in the sink by running water over it.

GTB0_short.text: Start the toaster. Once the lever pops up, take the bread to the plate on the dining counter.
Push down the lever of the toaster to turn it on.
Turn on the toaster. After the lever pops up, move the bread to the plate on the counter.
Start toasting. When the lever comes up, put the bread on the plate on the dining surface.
Turn the toaster on, and after the lever comes up, move the bread over to the plate on the dining counter.
Start the toaster by pushing the lever all the way down.
GTB0_short.source: 6. Start the toaster. Once the lever pops up, take the bread to the plate on the dining counter.
GTB0_short.why: Reuses the training clause 'Start the toaster' and adds the missing detail that the lever must go fully down.

GTB0_short.source: 6. Start the toaster. Once the lever pops up, take the bread to the plate on the dining counter.
GTB0_short.why: Uses the training wording nearly verbatim but keeps only the current step, so the policy does not move on to the bread yet.

GTB0_short.text: Press down on the toaster lever all the way to the bottom. Once finished, release the lever.
GTB0_short.source: 1. Pick up the sponge from the counter and clean the cutting board by briefly scrubbing or pressing down on the cutting board. Once finished, release the sponge.
GTB0_short.why: Borrows 'pressing down' and 'Once finished, release' and makes sure the lever is let go only after it reaches the bottom.

GTB0_short.text: Push the lever on the toaster fully down until it stays down, then release it.
GTB0_short.source: 6. Start the toaster. Once the lever pops up, take the bread to the plate on the dining counter.
GTB0_short.why: Corrects the three-quarter push by saying the lever must stay down before the gripper lets go.

GTB0_short.text: Start the toaster. Push the lever down past where it stopped before, all the way to the bottom.
GTB0_short.source: 6. Start the toaster. Once the lever pops up, take the bread to the plate on the dining counter.
GTB0_short.why: Reuses the training clause and points out that the earlier push was too short, so the stroke needs to go deeper.

GTB0_short.text: Press the toaster lever all the way down to start the toaster.
GTB0_short.source: 11. Pick the {obj} from the cabinet, place it under the coffee machine dispenser, and press the start button.
GTB0_short.why: Uses the 'press ... start' wording from the coffee task and applies it to pushing the lever fully down.

GTB1_short.text: Press down the toaster lever all the way to the bottom to start the toaster.

KB2_air.text: Pick the kettle from the counter and place it on a stove burner. Then turn the burner on.
Pick the kettle from the counter and place it on a stove burner.
Pick the kettle from the counter and place it on the stove.
Grab the kettle off the counter, set it onto a stove burner, and switch the burner on.
Take the kettle from the counter, move it to a stove burner, and turn the burner to on.
Pick up the kettle, set it down on a burner, and switch that burner on.
Pick the kettle from the counter and place it on a stove burner.
KB2_air.source: 7. Pick the kettle from the counter and place it on a stove burner. Then turn the burner on.
KB2_air.why: Reuses the first clause verbatim so the policy retries the grasp and placement it knows, without moving on to the knob yet.

KB2_air.text: Open the gripper, move to the kettle handle on the counter to the right of the stove, and pick the kettle up. Then place it on a stove burner.
KB2_air.source: 7. Pick the kettle from the counter and place it on a stove burner. Then turn the burner on.
KB2_air.why: The gripper closed on air, so it has to reopen and line up with the handle, which the wrist camera shows on the counter to the right.

KB2_air.text: Pick the kettle from the counter by its handle and place it on the empty burner on the right side of the stove.
KB2_air.source: 7. Pick the kettle from the counter and place it on a stove burner. Then turn the burner on.
KB2_air.why: Gives a grasp point and a clear placement target, the free right burner next to the pan.

KB2_air.text: Grab the kettle from the counter beside the stove and place it on a burner on the stove.
KB2_air.source: 13. Grab the pan from the cabinet and place it on the {knob} burner on the stove.
KB2_air.why: Uses the training grab-and-place structure with the kettle in place of the pan, stressing where the kettle is now.

KB2_air.text: Move closer to the kettle, close the gripper around its handle, and lift it off the counter. Then place it on a stove burner.
KB2_air.source: 7. Pick the kettle from the counter and place it on a stove burner. Then turn the burner on.
KB2_air.why: Corrects the miss: the last grasp landed beside the kettle, so it must get closer and make sure the handle is inside the gripper before lifting.

KB2_air.text: Pick up the kettle from the counter and place it on the stove burner. Once placed, release the kettle.
KB2_air.source: 1. Pick up the sponge from the counter ... Once finished, release the sponge.
KB2_air.why: Uses the pick-up and release phrasing to frame the whole sub-task through to letting go on the burner.
